terms.definition: Virtual Private Cloud — your own isolated, logically separated network within AWS where you control IP addressing, routing, and security
terms.example: Like a gated community inside the AWS city, where you decide who enters and who leaves

terms.definition: A smaller network segment carved from a VPC's IP address range, used to organize resources and control internet access
terms.example: Public subnet = street-facing units with front doors; private subnet = interior units with no direct outside access

terms.definition: Classless Inter-Domain Routing — notation like 10.0.0.0/16 that defines a range of IP addresses. The number after the slash controls the size of the range
terms.example: 10.0.0.0/16 gives 65,536 addresses; 10.0.1.0/24 gives 256 addresses

terms.definition: A VPC component that enables communication between resources in your VPC and the public internet
terms.example: Like the main entrance gate of a building that connects the inside to the outside world

terms.definition: A set of rules (routes) that determines where network traffic is directed within a VPC. Each subnet is associated with a route table
terms.example: Like a GPS system — it tells your data packet which path to take to reach its destination

terms.definition: A stateful, virtual firewall at the EC2 instance level that controls inbound and outbound traffic. Return traffic is automatically allowed
terms.example: Like a personal bodyguard for each EC2 instance — it checks who's allowed in and lets approved visitors leave freely

terms.definition: Network Access Control List — a stateless firewall at the subnet level. Both inbound and outbound rules must be explicitly set
terms.example: Like a checkpoint at the entrance to a neighborhood — everyone must show ID both entering AND leaving

terms.definition: A firewall property where response traffic is automatically allowed without needing explicit rules, because the connection state is tracked
terms.example: You knock on a door (inbound allowed) — stateful means you're automatically allowed to answer back (outbound auto-allowed)

terms.definition: A firewall property where every packet is evaluated independently with no memory of previous packets — both directions require explicit rules
terms.example: A strict guard who checks your ID every single time you pass through, both entering and leaving, regardless of previous visits

terms.definition: An AWS feature that captures metadata about IP traffic flowing to and from network interfaces in your VPC. Stores in CloudWatch Logs, S3, or Firehose
terms.example: Like a security camera log that records who entered, who was denied, and which door they used — but not what they said inside

terms.definition: A private networking connection between two VPCs that enables communication using private IP addresses without routing through the public internet
terms.example: Like building a private tunnel between two houses so you can visit each other without walking on the public road

terms.definition: VPC Peering only connects the two VPCs directly involved. If A peers with B, and B peers with C, A cannot reach C through B
terms.example: Road A connects Town A to Town B. Road B connects Town B to Town C. You still cannot drive from Town A to Town C without a direct Road C

terms.definition: A private connection between your VPC and supported AWS services that stays within the AWS network, requiring no internet gateway, NAT, or VPN
terms.example: Like a private staff entrance at a store — employees get direct access to the stockroom without using the public customer entrance

terms.definition: A type of VPC Endpoint that works only with S3 and DynamoDB, implemented as a route table entry, and is free of charge
terms.example: A free express lane on the highway that only buses (S3/DynamoDB traffic) can use

terms.definition: A type of VPC Endpoint powered by AWS PrivateLink that creates an ENI with a private IP in your subnet, supporting most AWS services
terms.example: A private dedicated phone line installed in your office that directly connects to AWS service offices without going through the public phone network

terms.definition: AWS technology that enables private, secure connectivity to AWS services, third-party services, and your own services using ENIs
terms.example: The underlying infrastructure that powers Interface Endpoints — think of it as the private fiber cable network inside the AWS building

terms.definition: Elastic Network Interface — a virtual network card attached to an EC2 instance or other AWS resource that has a private IP address
terms.example: Like a network port on a physical server — every network-attached device needs one to communicate

terms.definition: An AWS Systems Manager feature that provides browser-based shell access to EC2 instances without needing SSH keys, bastion hosts, or open port 22
terms.example: Like a secret internal intercom system that lets you talk to any room in the building without going through the front door

terms.definition: An AWS identity with specific permissions that can be assumed by AWS services or users to perform actions. Required when one AWS service needs to access another
terms.example: Like a staff pass that grants specific employees access to specific areas — the EC2 wears this pass to get permission to write to CloudWatch

terms.definition: An AWS network transit hub that enables transitive routing between thousands of VPCs, replacing the need for a complex mesh of VPC Peering connections
terms.example: Like a central train station — instead of building roads between every city pair, all cities connect to the one central hub

terms.definition: The time period over which VPC Flow Logs collect and aggregate traffic data before writing a log record. Options are 1 minute or 10 minutes
terms.example: A security guard writing a shift report every 1 minute vs every 10 minutes — more frequent reports = more granular visibility but more paper

terms.definition: An IAM resource-based policy attached to a VPC Endpoint that controls which AWS resources, principals, and actions are permitted through the endpoint
terms.example: A policy on the staff entrance that says 'only employees from the finance department may use this door, and only to access the finance storage room'
